{{Quote|You killed my family.''"<br />"''Casualties of war, kid.|[[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] and the Death Watch soldier|<ref name="OpenSeasons" />}}
A [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] '''Death Watch soldier''' fought against the [[True Mandalorians]] in a [[Battle of Concord Dawn|battle]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Concord Dawn/Legends|Concord Dawn]],<ref name="OpenSeasons" /> located in the [[Mandalore sector/Legends|Mandalore sector]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Together with the other members of the [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]], during the [[Lightfight|battle]], the soldier forced the True Mandalorians to retreat into the fields of locally grown crops. He then joined the [[Death/Legends|Death]] Watch [[Secret Mandalore|leader]],<ref name="OpenSeasons" /> [[Tor Vizsla]],<ref name="TEA" /> in hunting down the scattered True Mandalorians<ref name="OpenSeasons" /> and [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']] [[Jaster Mereel]].<ref name="HotM">{{InsiderCite|80|The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors}}</ref>

Upon tracking the True Mandalorians to the [[Clan Fett|Fett family]] [[Farm/Legends|farm]], violence broke out, leading to the deaths of the farm's [[Journeyman Protector/Legends|Journeyman Protector]] [[Fett (Elder Journeyman Protector)|owner]] and [[Jango Fett's mother|his wife]],<ref name="OpenSeasons" /> as well as the kidnapping of their daughter, [[Arla Fett]],<ref name="O66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref> events in which the Death Watch soldier took part. Though the True Mandalorians were able to save the family's young son, [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]], they were forced to flee again; this [[Time/Legends|time]], however, the Death Watch [[Fire/Legends|ignited]] the fields where the True Mandalorians were taking refuge, and as they burned, the Death Watch believed their foes had perished.<ref name="OpenSeasons" />

Thinking themselves victorious, the Death Watch soldier and his compatriots [[Tank/Legends|rode]] into a nearby [[City/Legends|town]] in order to celebrate, only to come under siege from a True Mandalorian ambush. Amidst the fighting, the Death Watch soldier was attacked by a vengeful Jango Fett. Held at blaster-point by the boy, Jango remebered the soldier as the one, alongside Vizsla, who killed his family but the Death Watch Soldier only gruffly retorted that the dead Fetts were "casualties of war". The Death Watch then attempted to kill the boy with his [[Armor/Legends|gauntlet's]] [[Vibroblade/Legends|vibroblade]]; slashing him across the face and knocking Jango to the ground. The Death Watch soldier prepared to finish him off only to be ultimately killed by the boy when Fett managed to grab a nearby blaster off the ground and [[Blaster/Legends|shoot]] the man in the chest, avenging his family. Fett was subsequently picked up and taken in Jaster's arms where he asked the young boy if he felt better. The traumatized, and confused, boy stated no — or more rather he didn't know. With that, Jaster welcomed him into the Mandalorians and eventually took Jango as his adoptive son.

==Behind the scenes==
The Death Watch soldier first appeared in ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] in the [[Jango Fett: Open Seasons 1|first issue]] of the [[Star Wars: Jango Fett: Open Seasons|''Jango Fett: Open Seasons'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic series]], written by [[W. Haden Blackman|Haden Blackman]] and published [[May 1]], [[2002]].
